title: name-clearance
description: THE SHAPE OF apps/<app>/name-clearance.json — the record `tooling/store/name-clearance.mjs --execute` writes and `tooling/ci/assert-name-clearance.mjs` reads. A clearance is a MEASUREMENT WITH A DATE, not a permanent fact: names get taken. The dating mechanism is not invented here — it is `{value, asOf, verify, verifyKind}` from Private/platform-state/schema/fact.schema.json, verbatim, with verifyKind:"remote" because that is precisely what tells a pre-commit hook not to dial out. Validated by tooling/app-yaml/schema-validate.mjs, whose implemented-keyword set is closed: a keyword this schema names and that validator does not implement is refused rather than skipped.

_why.description: Free prose. Present so a seeded record can carry the sentence that explains it without inventing a field.

app.description: The app slug this record belongs to. Must be the directory it sits in — a record filed under the wrong app is a clearance for somebody else's name.

slug.description: The lowercased identifier form of the name: the snap name, the AMO slug, the subdomain. Distinct from `app` because a rename changes this before it changes the directory.

name.description: THE FACT TRIPLE. `value` is the name that was cleared, and the guard compares it against apps/<app>/app.yaml's `name:`. A record for a different name is not a record.

verifyKind.description: ALWAYS `remote`, and the enum is closed to one value on purpose. Re-deriving a clearance means ~20 external calls over ~16.5 s. `remote` is the flag a hook reads to refuse to run it, which is the whole reason the field exists rather than the guard sniffing the command string.

asOf.description: The day the probes ran. Duplicated out of `name.asOf` so the staleness limb can age the RECORD even if the name triple is edited by hand.

overall.description: CLEAR — every channel that can answer said free. QUALIFIED — nothing blocks and something is owed (an owner ruling, a manual step). BLOCKED — a record was READ that holds the name on a channel that refuses duplicates. UNDETERMINED — coverage was lost on a globally-unique channel, which is not a pass.

controls.description: THE RED CONTROLS, PER CHANNEL, as measured on the run that wrote this record. `--execute` REFUSES to overwrite a good record with one whose controls failed: a stale-but-real clearance beats a fresh record full of "I could not check".

failed.description: Channel ids whose control did not come back. Non-empty means every verdict in this record is worth less than it looks, and the guard says so.

channels.description: One entry per channel in tooling/channel-register.json, keyed by its `id`. THE SET IS THE REGISTER'S, NOT A LIST KEPT HERE: a channel with no probe registered appears with verdict UNDETERMINED and says so, and is never silently absent.

verdict.description: THREE ANSWERS, NEVER TWO, plus the non-answer for a channel with no namespace. UNDETERMINED never counts as clear.

uniqueness.description: `global` — the store refuses a duplicate, so a hit is a wall. `tolerated` — a hit is a discoverability cost. `none` — no third party holds a name here. `UNKNOWN` — no probe is registered for this channel.

identifiers.description: THE PERMANENT IDENTIFIERS, which unlike names can never be changed or recycled once claimed. Every value here is read by tooling/ci/read-identity.mjs from the file tooling/channel-register.json declares — never synthesised from the name, because a name change that updates four of five files is exactly the defect [10]D-3 exists to catch.

trademark.description: ADVISORY SIGNAL ONLY. SOFTWARE CANNOT CLEAR A TRADEMARK AND THIS RECORD DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. Registry databases (USPTO TSDR, the UK IPO, the Indian registry) are not reachable from an unauthenticated read, and are not faked: an absence of evidence is recorded as an absence of evidence. `ruling: null` reads as QUALIFIED — never as a pass.

disclaimer.description: Printed verbatim by both the probe and the guard. It must say, in the output itself, that this is not legal advice.

ruling.description: ONLY THE OWNER WRITES THIS. null is not neutral: it is a finding that a dated ruling is owed.

basis.description: WHAT THE RULING RESTS ON — the decision record a reader opens to check it (`ADR 074`). Optional in the shape so a record written before the field existed still parses; tooling/ci/assert-name-clearance.mjs limb 7 refuses a non-null `ruling` without it. A whitespace-only string is refused here too (`pattern`), because a blank basis names nothing a reader can open.

ownerItem.description: The owner id that carries the owed ruling: a row of Private/platform-state/open.json such as `O-NAME-SUBLY-TRADEMARK`, or of the owner queue such as `A-12` (the id shape and the lookup are tooling/scripts/owner-ids.mjs). A null ruling with no owner item is a finding nobody owns, so the guard refuses it outright. tooling/scripts/assert-public-citations.mjs looks the id up in BOTH registers and refuses one that neither carries, one that both carry, and a live row whose text (`blocks` or `closes`, in open.json) never names this file's repo-relative path. Once `ruling` is recorded the id is provenance and holds nothing.

gatedUntil.description: THE BOUND ON THE OWNER GATE, and it is a bound rather than a waiver. While this date is in the future a null ruling PRINTS AS FAILING and does not block the build; on and after it, it blocks. It is written ONCE, by hand, and `--execute` PRESERVES it — a re-probe must never be able to extend its own gate, which is how a waiver outlives its reason.
